author: Bobby Grayson
description:
No README.md or NOTES.md edit was made on wf7/locals, per the round rules. Proposed text for the integrator, to be merged with the other branches' numbers.

README, in the "Supported subset" list (a new bullet after the init/1 bullet):

  - **Module-local functions.** A `def`/`defp` that is not a callback and
    that a callback reaches, directly or through another helper, becomes a
    Lean definition emitted before `beh`, named `<module>_<function>`; a call
    to it renders as a call. Its body must be in the pure fragment: `if`,
    `cond` and `case` as expressions, a block of bindings ending in a value,
    and everything the expression translator already renders. A helper that
    sends, spawns or logs has no effect the model could carry, so it is an
    error naming the helper -- once, not once per call site. Argument and
    result types come from a `@spec` when the module gives one and otherwise
    from the types the helper is called at. A helper that recurses on the
    tail of a list argument is an ordinary `def`; any other self-recursion
    takes a leading `fuel : Nat` and is called with the constant `localFuel`,
    which the generated file documents as an approximation. Mutual recursion
    is an error naming both helpers.

README, amending the init/1 bullet:

    `init/1` may now be a block: `Process.flag(:trap_exit, true)`, a PubSub
    subscribe, a `Logger` call (dropped), a call to a local helper, and
    bindings `v = e` of pure expressions, which are substituted into the
    state expression -- `init/1` has no Lean binder of its own, because the
    state is built at the spawn site. The option list a real `init/1` is
    handed is not modelled: a parameter used as one is the empty keyword
    list, so `Keyword.get(opts, :k, d)` is its literal default and the
    translator warns.

README, amending the untyped-mode paragraph:

    A module with no `@type state` and no `init/1` to infer one from now
    reads the shape off its callbacks' state patterns: a map pattern anywhere
    makes it a record whose fields are the keys the patterns match and the
    keys the bodies update or return, tuple patterns of one size make it
    positional, and patterns that only bind the state whole leave it the
    opaque `Term`.

README, Readiness section, numbers to fold in (wf7/locals alone, over the
five projects): blockers 1621 -> 1510; the family `call to a helper in the
same module` (271 occurrences in 41 modules, the largest) is replaced by
`local helper is not a pure expression` (254 in 40), which names a function
instead of a call site; `statement in init/1` 89/26 -> 21/15; `no @type state
and no init/1 to infer one from` 24/24 -> 5/5. Translatable modules stay 1.

NOTES, a paragraph for the round-7 section:

    The biggest single family in the readiness report was never the actor
    model: it was 271 calls to helpers in the same module. Translating them
    turned out to be a question about *where the error goes*. Inlining the
    helper at each call site would have reported the same defect 271 times;
    emitting each helper as its own Lean definition reports it once, at the
    definition, and says what stops it. That is the difference between a
    symptom list and a work list, and it is why the new family count (254) is
    barely lower than the old one (271) while the report is far more useful.
    The second lesson was about types. A helper has no declared type in
    Elixir, so its Lean signature has to come from somewhere: a `@spec` when
    there is one, and otherwise the types it is *called* at. Inferring from
    use needs the call sites rendered, and rendering them needs the
    signatures, so the translator renders everything three times -- the first
    round sees only the callbacks, the next two see the helpers calling each
    other at the types they now have -- and lets the definition fix its own
    result type before any use does, so one opaque call site cannot make a
    typed helper opaque.
title: Integrator record for wf7/locals: README/NOTES replacement text
